creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Decided and shipped as RED-9 (`docs/red/0009-shell-interpolation.md`), commit `f799ba47`.

The card framed this as two orthogonal features that must not be averaged: a quoting mechanism, and a shell-free argv form. Both shipped, plus a third form that was already there.

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `` $`literal {x}` `` | literal text is shell, interpolations are data |
| `$list` | argv - one word per element, exec`d directly, no shell |
| `$str_var` | raw - you built the string, you own it |

**Spellings rejected:** `{x:q}` and `{x!q}` (cryptic per `principles.md:7`, needs a grammar release, and puts escaping in a display-formatting slot); `shell_quote()` as the primary mechanism (see the superseded p0 card).

**The argv form cost nothing.** `grammar.js:1231` already has `$.list` under `literal` -> `primary_expr` -> `expr`, and `shell_cmd` takes `field("command", $.expr)` - a list command just errored at runtime. No new syntax, no tree-sitter release. It also runs on Windows, where `` $`...` `` does not.

**On the lint the card warned about:** no taint-scoped lint shipped, and the card`s concern was right - a warning on every interpolation would have landed where RAD30011 did (~73% of all hints, demoted to `--strict`). Instead RAD40023 fires only on interpolations wrapped in quotes the script wrote, which is a bounded migration set: 45 sites across 15 files in `~/src/scripts/bin`.

Implicit list splatting was chosen over an explicit spread (Nushell`s `...list`) because a list command was a hard error before, so there is no ambiguity to resolve and no behavior to preserve.
title: Decide the shell execution model: quoting primitive, argv form, or both
